notes.title: Super Bit Blaster XL
notes.content:
SUPER Bit Blaster XL is here! This version of Bit Blaster is improved in almost every way. New GFX, new controls, new enemies and more. Free to all previous Bit Blaster XL owners.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11525962/f267a53a944c4894ebb08ea23e6ed002b4960032.gif[/img]

I began creating Bit Blaster XL for Steam on a whim back in late 2015. I never could have imagined how its release would dramatically alter the direction of my life. These last few years in game development have provided me with so many amazing opportunities that I sometimes can't even believe them myself. I couldn't have done so much of this without the great support of a community that appeared out of nowhere to play my silly little arcade game.

Considering this update is so massive, I didn't want to upset the flow of the original game that people loved so much; so all previous owners of Bit Blaster XL will get a free upgrade to the new Super Bit Blaster XL and retain their copies of the original as well.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/865040/Super_Bit_Blaster_XL/

Super Bit Blaster XL is the next evolution Bit Blaster. Since it's release I have learned a lot more about Unity and C# and so I have reworked many aspects of the game. I added a new Co-Op mode, Vs Mode, improved the GFX, new translations, new Easter eggs, and various other new things. I also completely overhauled the control scheme due to feedback; while it's still not a Twin-Stick shooter, overall control is so much more responsive. 

I greatly appreciate your feedback and will do my best to ensure lengthy support for my games as usual. Please contact me through Twitter, My Website, Nickervision Studios Discord, or the forums if you want to discuss an issue with the game, something misleading on the store page, or you just want to say hello. 

-Adam Nickerson ([url=https://twitter.com/nickervision]@nickervision[/url])

notes.title: Secrets of the developer who sold half a million videogames you ve never heard of on Steam
notes.content:
In the space of a half-hour conversation, Adam Nickerson, aka Nickervision Studios, uses a variant of the phrase I don t know really how to make videogames at least half a dozen times. Yet he s managed to singlehandedly sell half a million copies of his games on PC.

You ve probably never heard of Bit Blaster XL, for example, but it s shifted 260,000 copies on Steam. He developed it solo, in just two weeks. Its follow-up, on course to be equally successful, was developed in 75 hours.

How did he do it? He figured out exactly how to get noticed on Steam during this time of seemingly ceaseless new releases – a time that has destroyed the hopes and dreams of many other small developers. (more…)

 [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/715010/Diamo_XL/] [b]Diamo XL[/b] [/url] is now available on Steam for PC, Mac, Linux.

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/615610] [b]orbt xl[/b] [/url] is now available on Steam for PC, Mac, Linux.
  
[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/615610] [b]orbt xl[/b] [/url] is my newest game I have adapted for the Steam platform, it is another score chasing, bite sized, arcade style game. The goal is to orbit around the blackhole while not colliding with an ever-increasing number of obstacles. There are a variety of skins to unlock for your planet and some good leaderboard fun to be had. I think if you enjoyed Bit Blaster XL you may enjoy orbt xl. 

Stay in orbit while avoiding obstacles or being sucked into a black hole. Survive as long as you can while dodging and weaving between the various obstacles, the closer you orbit to the center; the faster you achieve points. The longer you last, the harder it gets. The simple one button controls either increases or decreases your orbit as you press it or don’t.

Thanks to all of you for the great support of Bit Blaster XL I have managed to free myself a lot more time to make a lot of cool games this upcoming year. So, I hope you’ll give orbt xl a shot and if you like it, please leave a brief Steam review and share with friends/family as it will really help for the launch success of this game and allow me to keep progressing towards bigger and better things.

As always, please leave any feedback or suggestions you may have, it is with the communities help that Bit Blaster XL become such a solid experience and I want to ensure that happens with orbt xl as well.

notes.content:

[h1]Bit Blaster XL -  V3.00[/h1]
[list]
[*]The Bit Blaster XL Soundtrack by Spifftune is now available for FREE as DLC (includes one new track) [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/548700/]Get it here![/url]
[*]Reworked ALL in game menus to be more consistent and ‘professional’ across all menus. Can use either a keyboard, a mouse or a gamepad. I understand that the menus are only now in line with what videogames should all have at the most basic, but was a big deal for me to learn and code it to work this way. (please let me know if there are bugs) Looks less like it was designed by an amatuer in his garage studio. *cough*
[*]There is a new Bomb weapon in the game. Pressing ‘Y’ on the gamepad or ‘ALT’ on the Keyboard should activate it. Each ship has different amounts of bombs to start and they can be found randomly floating in space. There is also a bit of UI changes to show the new bomb setup in both the ship select screen and the gameplay UI. 
[*]The Laser power up is now nearly twice as long and far more effective, as well it has had at total overhaul to make it look cooler.
[*]The Magnet power up is now more powerful at pulling objects and costs less ammo while working and has had a slight GFX modification
[*]The Trail power up has been modified to make all singular trail bullets also move within their own small circles, really increasing the effectiveness of this power up
[*]The Heatseeking power up has been entirely rewritten and should now correctly reduce ammo as well as not double up or just disappear. It also now has a new look and a slight explosion upon collision that can take out multiple objects like the explode shot.
[*]Grow Shot has been modified to have Increased size of break-off bullets
[*]Through Shot has been modified to look more like a rail shot bullet, to hopefully better indicate that it goes through objects until it hits a wall
[*]Bounce Shot now has a slight green flash to it to set it apart from enemy bullets a little bit more while still remaining difficult enough to be balanced.
[*]Explode shot has had its rate of fire reduced slightly as well as has been shrunk slightly.
[*]Split shots rate of fire reduced slightly
[*]Bomb, Boost, and Shield pickups now look more impressive and should stand out better when things get a little crazy.
[*]Now fully supporting ultrawide displays and all sorts of bizarre resolutions. [*]Should now properly allow uncommon resolutions to be detected in video menu.
[*]Braking now uses half the resources as boost, allowing for much better control
[*]There are now increased Invincibility frames after losing a shield! The player will receive 1.5 seconds of immunity as well as a flashing ship to showcase it.
[*]The screen will now shake when you use a bomb, lose a shield, die, or crash into a wall. (a small changed but makes a huge impact)
[*]Resolved various spawning issues for Ultrawide displays, including but not limited to ammo spawning, enemy spawning, power up spawning and various GUI elements.
[*]Updated pause legend to have black background and new +Bomb pickup
[*]Updated all Text/Font in game and increased its clarity
[*]Optimized all textures to be better looking for all resolutions
[*]Modified powerups so they don’t spawn to close to walls
[*]Removed some unnecessary debug logs from here and there just to be cleaner
[*]The instructions for both auto and manual fire modes have been updated to reflect any changes.
[*]Bit Blaster XL is now using the latest version of Unity engine
I spent some time and cleaned up the Unity launcher binding labels to make it more easy to understand naming conventions (hopefully helping those who rebind controls)
[*]Enemy00’s Speed now increases as the round goes longer
[*]Enemy01a (small meteor bits) will now shrink, pop, and then despawn if they’ve spent too long floating on the screen instead of just disappearing.
[*]Enemy04 Now chases the player at an increasing speed as the game goes on, as well as taking shorter breaks each time it stops.
[*]Enemy05 Now stops and shoots bursts multiple times as it crosses the screen, with bigger bursts depending on how long its survived. Also has new effect showing charging up shot.
[*]Modified some mid-later round (20000+) balancing with enemy spawning and points allocation, to make the franticness a more balanced of a variety of enemies as well as more reasonable to allow average players to get higher achievements and expert players to get even further.
[*]Later in game rounds (35000+ points) will spawn more effective powerups for crowds far more often than the less powerful or utility power ups
[*]There is now slightly more time in between powerup spawns so multiple don’t wind up on the screen at the same time
[*]Ammo intro + tutorial enemy now spawn in a different location for better visibility
[*]Bit Blaster XL will now correctly run in the background when its window is not the focus
[*]Pause Menu Overhaul with new style menus
[*]Sound when ammo runs outs. Also blink red ammo
[*]Cleaned up nickervision support page and made buttons bigger and clearer
[*]Cleaned up garbage collection and resolved minor lag spikes
[*]Tidied up entire project behind the scenes. Removed redundancies, unused textures, out of date files and renamed many assets, making flow smoother.
[*]Upgraded to latest available Steamworks SDK and Steamworks.Net implementation
[*]Fixed alignment of some swapping GFX in instructions
[*]Bombs destroy powerups, but ammo stays.
[*]**New Leaderboard for V3.0 forward. The old V2.1 Scores are still saved, and you can still access V2.1 through the BETA tab in Steam if you prefer.**
[/list]
Thank you everyone for playing and sharing the game with your friends and family. Bit Blaster XL now has over 125,000 players, I am BLOWN away!.

If you are really enjoying Bit Blaster, make sure to leave a brief Steam Review and let others know to check it out.

-Adam Nickerson

Thanks to all of your feedback and suggestions I have added, changed, fixed and polished Bit Blaster XL into an even better game over the last ten months with the many successful patches and content releases.

Some of those changes includes; a new secondary bomb power up that can do some good old fashioned screen clearing explosions, some re-balanced endgame and point values to give a better median experience to all players and allowing experts to climb even higher, and a totally redesigned menu system that hopefully improves upon the currently terrible menus that feel like they were designed by some amateur in his garage studio *cough*. I should have a version in the BETA branch in the coming days so people can take a look and give me some feedback. (oh also, the soundtrack will be released as FREE DLC)

I really appreciate all the support and positivity. This experience with Bit Blaster XL on Steam has afforded me all sorts of amazing opportunities like attending E3 2016, Steam DevDays 2016, a visit to the Microsoft campus and much more.

notes.content:
I just wanted to provide a quick announcement to let all you Bit Blasters know that thanks to your support, reviews, and sharing the game with your friends, Bit Blaster XL has sold over 100,000 units on Steam. I am absolutely blown away by the love and support it's received. With it's overwhelmingly positive reviews and its incredibly helpful player community, it continues to reach more players every day. Thanks to all of your feedback and suggestions I have added, changed, fixed and polished Bit Blaster XL into an even better game over the last ten months with the many successful patches and content releases.

I have a new patch coming December 5th. I have tagged it as V3.0. It Includes a variety of fixes and changes that hopefully everyone will be pleased with. Some of those changes includes; a new secondary bomb power up that can do some good old fashioned screen clearing explosions, some re-balanced endgame and point values to give a better median experience to all players and allowing experts to climb even higher, and a totally redesigned menu system that hopefully improves upon the currently terrible menus that feel like they were designed by some amateur in his garage studio *cough*. I should have a version in the BETA branch in the coming days so people can take a look and give me some feedback. (oh also, the soundtrack will be released as FREE DLC)

I really appreciate all the support and positivity. This experience with Bit Blaster XL on Steam has afforded me all sorts of amazing opportunities like attending E3 2016, Steam DevDays 2016, a visit to the Microsoft campus and much more.

I can't thank you all enough for this experience and hope that I can share more great experiences with you into the future.

Adam Nickerson

notes.title: V2.03 BETA + Note From Developer
notes.content:
[h1]Note From Developer[/h1]
Hello again everyone. Just a quick bit of BETA testing before the next patch goes live. Full patch notes will be listed with the actual patch.

I have changed my game plan a little in the last week. A week ago I attended my first ever E3 in Los Angeles and it was amazing. I met a lot of really cool people that I had only ever read about and seen online (or in magazines when I was young). Also, somehow managing to get myself into the IGN after party was pretty damn amazing as well. Here's a couple of pictures of my time there for those interested:)

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11525962/3f7c97bffd8930dd7cf12de06319ba4923eef86b.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11525962/87fad8a5bd5b41930ecbbc91ce64497bdf6cb4cc.jpg[/img]

While the trip was a really great life experience, it was a wonderful business experience as well. It really opened my eyes to a lot of things. Through discussions with many other developers, big and indie alike, I discovered that I am actually doing very well for my first time dipping my toes in (for which I am very proud and thankful to you all). I also learned a lot about time management during/on development. Whether it was through the wisdom passed to me by others by their past experiences, or seeing current projects that had all sorts of problematic elements. It made me very aware that I needed to shift my focus. 

I had been working on a bigger feature that had been giving me a lot of trouble, it was Co-op. Since the game wasn't initially built with this in mind I had a lot of trouble getting it working smoothly. So I have now rolled back all the work I did on that (I took great notes for the future though). That's not to say Co-op won't ever happen, but I wanted to make sure I was getting tangible patches into players hands ASAP. Especially since there were some outstanding features and fixes I had been wanting to resolve for a variety of reports/requests. Making you the players wait for a bigger patch seems pointless. I got caught up in the Vanity of large and feature ritch patch notes, when in actuality, what seems to be minor improvements like a pause feature and more responsive controls are huge to the players right now. 

I don't even know if I needed to write all this out or if it really matters in any way, but i'd rather have the game working its best and in players hands ASAP and it really helps to just write out my thoughts about it for those that have any interest.

So I am putting a patch up in the BETA branch, which will probably go live in the public branch once myself and others have done a few hours of testing. Thanks for sticking with me on my learning experience.

Adam Nickerson

I also learned a lot about time management during/on development. Whether it was through the wisdom passed to me by others by their past experiences, or seeing current projects that had all sorts of problematic elements. It made me very aware that I needed to shift my focus. 

I had been working on a bigger feature that had been giving me a lot of trouble, it was Co-op. Since the game wasn't initially built with this in mind I had a lot of trouble getting it working smoothly. I don't even know if I needed to write all this out or if it really matters in any way, but i'd rather have the game working its best and in players hands ASAP and it really helps to just write out my thoughts about it for those that have any interest.

notes.title: ★ Update from the Developer ★
notes.content:
[h1][b]To my fellow Bit Blasters![/b][/h1]

First of all, I'd like to say a big [b]THANK YOU[/b] to everyone that has played, shared, supported and rated Bit Blaster XL since its release on Steam in January. It really means a lot to me as a solo, still learning developer that so many people are enjoying my game. Thank you so so much!

I just wanted to put a couple bullet points out there to express some amazing (or at least I think so) facts and milestones in Bit Blaster XL's journey over its first five months on Steam.
[list]
[*][b]40,000+[/b] players worldwide (that's crazy to me)
[*][b]99% Overwhelmingly Positive[/b] review status on Steam, sometimes even topping out as the highest on average reviewed title available on the Steam platform (this is thanks to everyone's constant kind words and awesome reviews)
[*]Many patches and hot fixes since release, including everything from bug fixes, new modes (manual fire), leader boards, more achievements, new ships to unlock, new power ups, new enemies, new music, rewritten movement system, and many other significant graphical and game play improvements
[*]An incredibly helpful and active community helping me track down every last bug and issue in the game as well as suggest great new features and improvements to add
[*]A huge amount of wicked posts, comments and articles on many press sites, Reddit and Twitter
[/list]
Over the last month or so I have been focusing mostly on my day job (I am a self employed IT guy) while keeping an eye on Bit Blaster XL forums to ensure anyone having a problem could get some help. I recently bought my first Condo with my GF and moved/set up my office at my new home. Here is a little preview of my modest space...[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11525962/6c1be67cf5df3c4aa6479950d7afd9f8aefce64b.jpg[/img] I still have yet to hang my last few posters (waiting for my HL2 one to finish being framed). I also needed to make some time to play some new games, Stardew Valley (basically my dream game when I was growing up), Uncharted 4 (was a stellar conclusion), and even toying around with my new HTC Vive and a variety of the software that comes with that (check out Job Simulator, The Lab, and Space Pirate Trainer)

Now that I am settled in at my new place (mostly) I am ready to get back to working on the next significant patch for Bit Blaster XL. I wanted to keep everyone in the loop so that you all know I am still around and reading your ideas and suggestions and taking notes all while doing the best I can to provide customer support to anyone having issues. I don't yet have a date for when I will be releasing the next patch, as I intend to take my time and look harder into some things that have really confounded me in the past. 

I can offer no guarantees for what will or won't make it into the patch, but I am certainly looking hard at things suggested to me by the community including;
[list]
[*]Pause system
[*]Static backgrounds to liven up the environment, without impacting the play
[*]Steam cloud for saves
[*]In-game resolution and windowed mode options
[/list]
Please keep in mind, I am just learning as I go, so I cannot promise these will ever actually make it in, just know that I am going to do my damndest to look into implementing them if I can.

On top of those things above, I have my own list of changes / additions I will be making (ones I know for sure I can code) These changes include things like; an entirely new mode, additional underlying systems of game play to add more strategy to the experience (while still being able to play exactly how you do now too if you want), along with some great small fixes, graphical additions and game play enhancements.

I just want to say [b]thank you[/b] again for all the support so far. Hopefully Bit Blaster XL can continue to make an impact with players looking for a fun retro arcade game experience. I hope that this eventually turns into me being able to work on games as my day job instead of it just a hobby. I can only imagine the things I could learn and create with the extra time, especially with an awesome community like you all offering feedback along the way.

Oh also, [b]Bit Blaster XL will be on the week long sale on Steam starting next Monday for 50% off[/b], that's as low as $0.49 cents in many markets, so selling the trading cards will literally(probably) pay you back. Please don't hesitate to share Bit Blaster XL with your friends and family, your favorite press sites and Youtubers, or leave a brief review on Steam if you have yet to do so, letting others know what you like about it. It all really helps me to continue to make games and make them the best I can.

Adam Nickerson

notes.title: V2.02
notes.content:
[h1]Bit Blaster XL - V2.02 Patch Notes: (fixes and small changes)[/h1]
[b]-->  [/b]Resolved crash on startup due to leaderboard queries
[b]-->  [/b]Default resolution issues; modified to open by default in borderless window, as well as support more resolutions.
[b]-->  [/b]Resolved Achievement for ship08 not always activating correctly.
[b]-->  [/b]Added a version number to main menu for better bug reporting/detection in the future
[b]-->  [/b]Magnet and Bulletshield sounds should now correctly respond to audio settings.
[b]-->  [/b]Changed splash screen transitions to not be so sudden
[b]-->  [/b]Moved ‘more games by nickervision’ to thank you/exit screen and changed note.
[b]-->  [/b]sharpened all GFX assets to a slightly higher resolution
[b]-->  [/b]Fixed issue where going back to main menu from end game screen you could occasionally see enemies glitch.
[b]-->  [/b]spacebar can now play another round from gameover screen.
[b]-->  [/b]Either CTRL, ALT, or X keyboard keys can be used to shoot in manual mode. (as well as controller X)
[b]-->  [/b]added correct menu sound effects for vsync, autofire, and vibrate toggles.

[h1]V2.00 Patch Notes: (more songs, powerups, manual fire, OH MY!)[/h1]
[b]-->  [/b]New songs added by Spiff Tune; now there are unique songs for each ship.
[b]-->  [/b]New mode; Autofire mode can be enabled/disabled at the ship select screen. Will allow the player to hold “CTRL” or “X” on gamepad to shoot. The shooting is still tied to the ship’s and active power up’s rate of fire, but allows the player more control over their ammo usage if they so choose. Manual shooting mode will track separate local high scores for each ship as well.
[b]-->  [/b]New Passive Power up #1 - Magnet; shoots normal bullets but attracts all ammo and coins at more than three times the speed.
[b]-->  [/b]New Passive Power up #2 - BulletShield; has four round bullets floating around your ship protecting you from close calls and spins faster while boosting.
[b]-->  [/b]New Player Ship 08; Max stats of four shields, four speed, and four rate of fire. Also has hidden passive ability to gain double ammo with each pickup.
[b]-->  [/b]New Steam Achievement for unlocking Ship 08.
[b]-->  [/b]New Steam Leaderboard for players using Manual Fire.
[b]-->  [/b]New enemy 06; A big enemy that breaks apart in the same fashion as enemy 01, but has four bullet shields floating around it that absorb most shots, once the core enemy gets destroyed, the enemy breaks apart and the bullet shields fly at the player.
[b]-->  [/b]Modified explode shot slightly to have a bigger blast radius and slightly longer fuse.
[b]-->  [/b]Re-Balanced some enemy spawning and appearances below 20,000 points.
[b]-->  [/b]Modified the power up pickups GFX to look a little more obviously power up-ish
[b]-->  [/b]Re-Balanced the cost for ships slightly and added new ship to menu. Now (5,10,20,30,40,50,100).
[b]-->  [/b]Upon purchasing all ships, the coin collection indicator will disappear from ship selection screen but will still track coin collection in the background in case more coin purchases are added in the future.
[b]-->  [/b]Correctly updating the highscores list directly after earning a new highscore.

Thank you everyone for playing and sharing the game with your friends and family. If you are really enjoying Bit Blaster, make sure to leave a Steam Review and let others know.

-Adam Nickerson

notes.title: Bit Blaster XL V1.10 BETA Patch
notes.content:
Hey Everyone,

I just wanted to send through an announcement of the V1.1 BETA patch now being available in the BETA branch for Win32, Win64, Linux32, Linux64, OSX.

It features a variety of fixes and improvements. I would love if some players could test it out and let me know that it works. If you do test it, please leave feedback in a comment below (good or bad) with whatever important/unique details you can provide about your machine (Operating system, 32 or 64 bits, 60hz, 120hz, etc)

To try out the BETA version of Bit Blaster XL V1.1, just [b]right click the game in the library tab. --> Click Properties --> Click the BETAS tab --> from the Drop down box select the Testing beta.[/b]  It should then automatically download. Make sure that if the BETA doesn't work for you, you use the same method to turn it off.

[b]Some of the fixes include:[/b]
-All Objects should now move at the same speed regardless of framerate
-Super fast gameplay and super slow gameplay should now be resolved
-Heatseeker should work great now
-Fully rewritten shield system, should be far more stable and allow for a couple upcoming features
-Mouse cursor should now disappear correctly during a round of play and reappear in menus.
-Slightly adjusted colors here and there, and modified various GUI details ever so slightly. 
-And a variety of other small changes. 

Of course I don't want to push this until I have a good handful of people from a variety of machines telling me its working great. Many people have shared videos with me too and that's always very helpful as well, send them to info(at)nickervision(dot)com

And lastly, thank you to everyone that has been playing so far, left great reviews, and share Bit Blaster XL with their friends and family. This launch week has far exceeded my expectations and it feels great to be embraced by such an awesome community. [b]Thanks so so much.[/b]

-Adam Nickerson

notes.title: V1.02
notes.content:
[h1]Bit Blaster XL - V1.02 Patch Notes:[/h1]

[b]-> [/b]Bit Blaster V7 Achievement should now correctly activate. (including retroactively to anyone that had already earned it.
[b]-> [/b]The skybox and other various details should now appropriately scale to the outrageously sized 21:9 monitors :)
[b]-> [/b]Dead zone on gamepad issues should now be resolved. (dpad is not in use currently due to my own programming limitations, will hopefully be back in the future)
[b]-> [/b]The Orange "H" powerup will now correctly find targets, if the target is destroyed, it will find a new target, if no targets available it will disappear. Should also no longer get jammed and need a game restart to work again.
[b]-> [/b]I have discovered how to manage the questionable leaderboard scores and will do my best to remove all the ones that are completely outrageous.
[b]-> [/b]I added a slight acceleration to keyboard left and right controls allowing the player a little tighter control.
[b]-> [/b]When dying while boosting, the booster would auto be on next life, this has now been fixed.
[b]-> [/b]I have correctly added both the Windows 32 bit builds and Linux 32 bit builds so that people having trouble booting the game should now be able to play.
[b]-> [/b]Please make sure to check the discussions board for a stickied post where I will do my best to track all issues.

Thank you everyone for the feedback; this has been a wonderful experience and a super intense 36 hours to start the launch. I will do my best to fix any issues you encounter and post in the discussion thread or email me info(at)nickervision.com.

I want to thank everyone for the AWESOME reviews you've been leaving. As well as all you that are sharing the game with friends and family. You're all very kind and it makes me feel absolutely amazing that you are enjoying a goofy little game I made. :)
